precepts.text: The days of our years are threescore years and ten, and if by reason of strength fourscore, yet is their strength labour and sorrow, and we fly away. Take care of the temple so God may be merciful with the eighty.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.
precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten”: seventy years is what we have. “and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years”: if God is merciful, we might get eighty years out of this body. You know the Bible is a true book: you get to hitting around forty and you say, damn, David was right.

That's why Captain Gideon did the class about working out, not drinking sodas and calcifying the bones, eating once a day and taking good care of yourself, so God can be merciful: he did real good with that temple I gave him; let me give him eighty years.

“yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” We fly away means the spirit goes back to its Creator. That is the one day a man is going to fly: when he gets up out of this body.

And even eighty years is nothing to God. Peter says one day with the Lord is as a thousand years; by that measure a whole human lifetime is less than two hours in God's eyes, and it could be even less. Your life is but a vapor. So how do you look down on others and think so highly of yourself? Think soberly, and humble yourself.

precepts.text: Our days are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore years; the beauty of youth does not last the span.
precepts.point: Favour is deceitful and beauty is vain. You are not going to look the same at seventy that you did at twenty-five; our days are threescore years and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore, and outside a handful who retain a semblance of their youth, the looks fade along the way. A woman that feareth the Lord, she shall be praised.

note.label: Genesis 29: Bone and Flesh in Haran

precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.”

Set that span against beauty. Seventy years, or eighty by reason of strength; and outside a handful who retain a semblance of their youth, the looks fade along the way. You are not going to look the same at seventy that you did at twenty-five. The beauty of youth does not last the span, which is why favour is deceitful and beauty is vain, and why Jacob loving Rachel more than Leah for her looks was building on something that passes.

precepts.text: The days of our years are threescore and ten, or by reason of strength fourscore years; a man is very aged at seventy and eighty.
precepts.point: A quarrel then arose between the men of Israel and the men of Judah over who had the right to bring the king back. Judah claimed the king was near of kin to them, being of the tribe of Judah, while Israel claimed ten parts in the king and more right in David, and the words of Judah were fiercer than the words of Israel. This was the tribe strife that would later split the northern and southern kingdoms, though they were all Israel.

note.label: 2 Samuel 19: The King Returns to His House

precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” A man is very aged at seventy and eighty.

Barzillai was fourscore, the span given by reason of strength, and his strength was labour and sorrow: “can I discern between good and evil? can thy servant taste what I eat or what I drink? can I hear any more the voice of singing men and singing women?” He would not be a burden to the king, so he sent Chimham over with David in his place, and the king kissed him and blessed him, and he returned unto his own place.

precepts.text: The Lord possessed Christ in the beginning of His way, set up from everlasting, before the mountains were settled.
precepts.point: We are like grass which groweth up; in the morning it flourisheth and groweth up, in the evening it is cut down and withereth. Our youth is like a blade of grass, green and healthy, but the glory of it fades away.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
“Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.” Proverbs speaks of the one who was with him then: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was. When there were no depths, I was brought forth; when there were no fountains abounding with water. Before the mountains were settled, before the hills was I brought forth”.

The Lord possessed Christ in the beginning of his way, set up from everlasting, before the mountains were settled. The same words Moses uses of the Most High, before the mountains, from everlasting, are used of Christ being brought forth.

So the Lord who has been our dwelling place in all generations has been God from everlasting, and Christ was with him before the earth was.

precepts.text: My spirit shall not always strive with man; his days shall be a hundred and twenty years, as He constantly cuts our days short.
precepts.point: The days of our years are threescore years and ten; a score is twenty, so three score and ten is seventy. At seventy you must give up the ghost, for the Lord's spirit will not always be striving with you.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
“The days of our years are threescore years and ten; and if by reason of strength they be fourscore years, yet is their strength labour and sorrow; for it is soon cut off, and we fly away.” A score is twenty, so threescore and ten is seventy. At seventy you must give up the ghost, for the Lord's spirit will not always be striving with you.

That goes back to the flood: “And the Lord said, My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh: yet his days shall be an hundred and twenty years.” His spirit shall not always strive with man, and man's days were set at a hundred and twenty years. He constantly cuts our days short, from a hundred and twenty down to seventy or eighty.

We are consumed by his anger, and he has set our iniquities before him, our secret sins in the light of his countenance. That is how the Lord can judge you; we don't get away. In the regeneration they shall live again, and then the works of the righteous and the works of the wicked shall be declared. Our years are spent as a tale that is told.

precepts.text: Make me to hear joy and gladness, that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
precepts.point: He asks that His work appear unto His servants and His glory unto their children, that the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and that He establish the work of our hands. The Lord will give us according to the fruit of our doings.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
Moses prays, “O satisfy us early with thy mercy; that we may rejoice and be glad all our days. Make us glad according to the days wherein thou hast afflicted us, and the years wherein we have seen evil.” David prays the same after his own affliction: “Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.”

The bones the Most High has broken are the days wherein he afflicted us and the years wherein we have seen evil. The prayer is that the gladness match the affliction, that the broken bones themselves rejoice. Satisfy us early with mercy, and let the same hand that broke us make us glad.

precepts.text: I the Lord search the heart, to give every man according to his ways and the fruit of his doings, so our doings must be the fruit of the spirit.
precepts.point: He asks that His work appear unto His servants and His glory unto their children, that the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us, and that He establish the work of our hands. The Lord will give us according to the fruit of our doings.

note.label: Psalm 90: Teach Us to Number Our Days

precepts.why:
Moses asks that “the beauty of the Lord our God be upon us: and establish thou the work of our hands upon us; yea, the work of our hands establish thou it.” Jeremiah shows how the Lord decides what to establish: “I the Lord search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.”

The Lord will give us according to the fruit of our doings. He searches the heart and tries the reins, so the work of our hands is established only if it is the right fruit. Our doings must be the fruit of the spirit.

That is the condition on the prayer. If we want his work to appear unto his servants and his glory unto our children, the work of our hands has to be work he can establish.
